label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1011b29-1012a1: In respect of a contradictory pair, every change goes…
interpretation: The dilemma against the intermediate: it is either like grey between black and white, or like what is neither man nor horse. On the second horn it would not change, 'for change is from not good to good or from this to not good' (ἐκ μὴ ἀγαθοῦ γὰρ εἰς ἀγαθὸν μεταβάλλει ἢ ἐκ τούτου εἰς μὴ ἀγαθόν). On the first horn there would be a generation to white not from not-white, 'but this is not seen'. Both horns rest on one premise, read here: in respect of a contradictory pair every change goes from one side to the other. Only the direction from change to its two termini is taken; the wider parenthesis (no change except into opposites and intermediates) concerns contraries and is not used. Formalized over states, a predicate F and a change relation (TruthCore.Greek.Aristotle.Metaphysics.ChangeOnlyBetweenContradictoriesReading). Fidelity: read constructively, the premise is a disjunction about every change, so whoever grants it has already granted that each changing state is on one side; this is where an intuitionist withholds.
